run: weather capitalize — CAPACITY vs the champion (the decisive comparison)
question: can weather be brought to at least the champion's level?

measured_live_books.read: weather's spread is ~2x the champion's and its book is ~8x thinner at the median; the champion has a fat right tail (mean $15k, 35% of books >$1k) that weather ENTIRELY LACKS (0% >$1k). The book is the binding constraint, not the edge.

capacity_model.basis: turnover = signals/day x fillable $ within 1c of the touch; gross = turnover x ROI-turn LB

VERDICT.can_weather_reach_champion_level: NO — not on CAPACITY, and it never can. The book physically isn't there (~$54/signal vs ~$427, 0% of weather books hold >$1k vs 35% of the champion's).
VERDICT.but: weather's PER-DOLLAR edge is ~2x the champion's (LB +11.1% at the measured 3c half-spread, LODO held-out +9.4%, vs the champion's +5.6% floor). So it delivers ~50% of the champion's dollar output on only ~26% of its turnover.
VERDICT.therefore: weather is a CAPACITY-CAPPED SATELLITE SLEEVE, not a champion replacement. Run it ALONGSIDE the champion (low-correlated, stably positive daily) for roughly +50% on total output — do not try to scale it INTO the champion's role.
VERDICT.implement_as: the BLIND BAND rule, NOT the consensus arm: B3 showed consensus adds +0.14pp (i.e. nothing) while COSTING signals. Blind band gives 52.5 sigs/day vs 44.1 — ~19% more capacity at the same edge, and it is simpler (no consensus machinery).
VERDICT.the_real_engineering: the binding constraint is the BOOK, so the work is a SLIPPAGE-AWARE SIZER (take only what the book gives within a 1c budget), NOT a better selector. Selection is done.
